Title: Sikkim: Indian Army's Operation Sadbhavana Unites Border Villages Through Football
Original Text:
GANGTOK: The Indian Army sponsors a football game­ at a high altitude, bringing together borde­r villages. This part of their program, Operation Sadbhavana, aims for unity in East Sikkim.

The­ Trishakti Corps from the Indian Army started a unique ide­a for unity and friendship. As part of Operation Sadbhavana, a friendly football game­ was set up. The teams we­re from the border village­s of Gnathang and Kupup in East Sikkim. The game was held 12,600 fe­et above sea le­vel which added a special touch. It took place­ under the beautiful sky of East Sikkim. This was a cle­ar sign of the army’s dedication to promoting patriotism and teamwork in the­se border regions.

Local youngste­rs eagerly joined the­ event which showed it was a hit. It cre­ated a feeling of fun, unity, and re­spect for each other. Fans from both village­s supported their teams showcasing gre­at sportsmanship. The locals were grate­ful for the army’s effort in creating e­vents like these­ which builds trust and fosters good relationships in these­ border areas.

The Ope­ration Sadbhavana program, focusing on helping the community, has had a positive impact on the­ lives of these village­rs. A prize ceremony took place­ after the football game. This was a spe­cial part of the program. The players we­re praised for their skills, spirit, fitne­ss, and devotion to the game. The­ ceremony not only awarded individual e­fforts but also highlighted the idea that sports contribute­ to unity and friendship.

A high-altitude football game­ turned out to be a huge success. It showed the­ Indian Army's hard work in creating good vibes and strong bonds with civilians in the tough and far-flung re­gions lining the Indo-China border. This is because­ of Operation Sadbhavana. The Indian Army continually shows it's all-in for peace­ and unity in the border villages of Sikkim. The­y leave a dee­p and enduring impression on the he­arts and minds of the locals.

Title: Major Dwipannita Kalita, Indian Army officer from Assam, featured in Femina's special edition
Original Text:
Major Dwipannita Kalita hails from Dhekiajuli in Assam and joined the Indian Army after completing her MBBS in the Philippines and then working in a hospital in Delhi before choosing the olive and green uniform of the Army

Assam Army officer Major Dwipannita Kalita featured in Femina’s special edition on Women Army officers ~ A woman Army officer from Assam has made her way to a special list of 10 distinguished women Army bravehearts and has been featured by eminent fashion magazine Femina in a special edition on women donning the olive and green outfit.

Major Dwipannita Kalita hailing from Dhekiajuli, Assam, who had earlier made her way into the recordbooks by becoming the first female paratrooper from the State, has been featured on the cover of Femina India’s Independence Day Special Edition titled “Warrior Women of the Indian Army” alongside nine other women officers of the Indian Army.

The other women Army bravehearts who have been featured in Femina’s special edition includes Colonel Sofia Qureshi who had briefed the nation on Operation Sindoor, the diabolic military strikes on terror bases inside Pakistan to avenge the deaths of 26 people killed in the Pahalgam terror attack.

The special August edition honours “the strength, discipline, and unflinching courage of all the women who serve in the Indian Army”, Femina stated, and added: “These 10 women warriors represent the evolving face of India’s defence forces. They lead from the front, with an unwavering spirit, standing guard so the rest of us can live free”.

Major Kalita hails from Dhekiajuli in Sonitpur district of Assam and is one of the few members of the Army Medical Corps who make up the elite Parachute Medical Regiment.

Her journey from modest sorroundings of Dhekiajuli to the Indian Army has been a tale of grit and determination. After completing her MBBS in the Philippines, she worked in emergency and obstetrics and gynecology departments of a hospital in Delhi before joining the Indian Army.

In her free time, Major Kalita loves spending time in the gym while her other favourite pastimes are cooking with soft jazz music playing in the background, and playing with her dogs.

She also loves gardening.

Meanwhile, Major Dwipannita Kalita making it to the cover of Femina’s special edition has led to a buzz in social media back home in Assam.

Taking to his ‘X‘ account, Dhekiajuli MLA and Assam Health Minister Ashok Singhal wrote: Incredibly proud to see Major Dwipannita Kalita, a daughter of Dhekiajuli and the first female paratrooper from Assam, featured on the cover of Femina India, alongside Colonel Sofia Qureshi and 8 other valiant Veeranganas of the Indian Army.”

Along with Major Kalita from Assam and Colonel Sofiya Qureshi, Colonel Ponung Doming from Pasighat in Arunachal Pradesh has also been featured in the special Independence Day edition of Femina.

Title: Indian Army, Assam Rifles ensure protection to vehicles on national highway in violence-hit Manipur
Original Text:
As the state of essential supplies in violence-hit Manipur began to dwindle and reach critical levels, the India Army and Assam Rifles have been working in close coordination with utmost synergy to assure protection to vehicles carrying essential goods to and from Imphal, officials said.

Towards this, Army and Assam Rifles in conjunction with the state government, Manipur Police and CAPFs have been working in close coordination and synergy to assure protection to vehicles via NH 37, “The Lifeline of Manipur”.

“At any given point of time while the movement of vehicles is being undertaken prophylactic Area Domination Patrols of Army and Assam Rifles, Quick Reaction Teams operating from Company Operating Bases located astride NH 37, aerial surveillance by Unmanned Aerial Vehicles and Cheetah Helicopters, Companies of CRPF, Manipur Police personnel from five police stations alongwith persons from India Reserve Battalion are tasked to ensure security of civilian vehicles plying on NH 37,” Indian Army said.

Further, to guarantee dedicated security, vehicles are also accompanied by Quick Reaction Teams of Manipur Police and CRPF.

According to the Indian Army, the movement on NH 37 commenced with effect on May 15 and is a result of tedious planning and synergy at the grassroot level.

“Security Forces remain committed to restoring complete normalcy and the commencement of movement of the vehicles on NH 37 is another step towards normalcy in Manipur,” the Army officials said.

Earlier on May 18, the India Army and Assam Rifles stepped in to assure protection to vehicles carrying essential goods to and from Imphal, informed Indian Army officials.

According to the Indian Army, a convoy of 28 vehicles including trucks, fuel tankers, and JCB carrying rice, sugar, pulses and fuel moved under the escort of CRPF and Manipur Police from Noney to Imphal.

Prophylactic domination of the area was provided by Assam Rifles to ensure safe passage to the convoy which reached Imphal safely by afternoon,” stated Indian Army officials.

In addition, monitoring was also ensured through unmanned aerial vehicles, informed officials.

“Together for Peace in #Manipur” Movement of vehicles on NH 37 commenced from 15 May. The same ensured beefing up of essential supplies, levels of which were gradually dwindling. #IndianArmy and #AssamRifles are committed to safely move through troops on ground & aerial surveillance,” Tweeted SpearCorps Indian Army.

Normalcy is slowly returning to Manipur after violence left 70 people dead and 1,700 houses were burnt down.

As per the latest figures, close to 71 people lost their lives while more than 230 were injured and close to 1700 houses were burnt down during the violence in Manipur.

Title: Indian Army Unveils Trophy for Captain Jintu Gogoi Football Tournament on Vijay Diwas 2024
Original Text:
DIBRUGARH: Indian Army unveiled the coveted trophy for the Captain Jintu Gogoi Football Tournament on the momentous occasion of Vijay Diwas 2024. This tournament is named after the the braveheart from Golaghat, Assam, Captain Jintu Gogoi, who made the supreme sacrifice during the Kargil War 1999. The tournament is designed to ignite the spirit of competition and camaraderie among the youth of the region.

The grand unveiling ceremony took place in Digboi, orchestrated by the Laipuli Brigade of the Red Shield Division. This brigade holds a remarkable legacy, having played a pivotal role in the 1971 operations on the Eastern Front and is also known as the Albert Ekka Brigade, in tribute to Lance Naik Albert Ekka who was awarded the Paramvir Chakra for his extraordinary bravery during the Battle of Gangasagar.

The event was graced by enthusiastic young footballers from local schools in Digboi, alongside team captains and managers from various participating clubs. This year tournament will showcase an exhilarating participation of 12 teams from across Assam. Matches will unfold at multiple venues in Tinsukia, culminating in a grand finale at Duliajan.

Title: Indian Army Hosts Agniveer Recruitment Rally in Udalguri
Original Text:
MANGALDAI: The Indian Army has been conducting an Agniveer Recruitment Rally at Upendranath Brahma Football Stadium, Udalguri from August 16 to August 23. This rally is aimed at selecting candidates from the North Eastern States with focus on districts of Lower Assam and is one of the biggest recruitment events organized in the region.

Approximately, 25,000 candidates had appeared in the written exam this year from which 2,500 candidates from 13 districts of Assam and seven Northeastern states were shortlisted for this recruitment rally. The rally is being conducted for candidates from the districts of Baksa, Chirang, Barpeta, Goalpara, Bongaigaon, Dhubri, Darrang, Udalguri, Kamrup Metro, Kamrup Rural, Kokrajhar, Nalbari and South Salmara and from all seven North Eastern states for recruitment of soldiers and Junior Commission Officer (Religious Teacher).

The rally presents a unique opportunity for young and eligible candidates to join the Indian Army as Agniveers, serving the nation with distinction. Eligible candidates from the North Eastern States are invited to participate in this rally and take advantage of this opportunity to become part of the Indian Army.

Title: Roles of Indian Army and Assam Rifles in tackling insurgency in Tripura lauded
Original Text: Silchar: Tripura, a State that has recently emerged out of more than two decades of insurgency, is fast gaining importance on the strategic index of the North. Over the years, the State has witnessed combined effect of the efforts of Assam Rifles and Indian Army in the restoration of peace and normalcy during the bloody years of insurgency as also subsequently to create an environment conducive for the peace to prosper. The wide array of civic action programs conducted jointly by army and Assam Rifles have assisted the State government as well as local administration in enhancing their outreach to the remotest corners of the State. During flood relief operations of 2018, the Armed Forces present in Tripura worked relentlessly to save more than 1200 precious lives and assisted in the distribution of relief materials.
